title: SMS gateway client with Polly retries
name: SMS gateway sender

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code makes retried sends to the SMS gateway safe? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
The gateway answers a send with HTTP 400 because the phone number is malformed. What happens to that message in DispatchPendingAsync?
choices: It is retried up to four more times with exponential backoff, then released for a later batch.
It is retried once, because 4xx responses get a single immediate retry.
It is sent once, SendAsync returns Rejected, and the store marks it rejected with status 400.
SendAsync throws HttpRequestException, which the dispatcher catches and releases for later.

questions.prompt: The gateway accepts connections but never responds. Roughly how long can one SendAsync call for a single message take before it returns a result or throws?
choices: About 3 seconds, since the timeout strategy bounds the whole call.
Around 15 seconds of attempt timeouts plus several seconds of backoff delays, because the timeout applies to each attempt.
Indefinitely, because the HttpClient has no timeout configured and the pipeline cannot override it.
About 0.4 seconds, because the first failure aborts and the delays only apply to HTTP status failures.

questions.prompt: The gateway returns 429 with a Retry-After header of 120 seconds on the first attempt. How long does the pipeline wait before the second attempt?
choices: About 400 ms plus jitter, since the header is ignored for 429 responses.
Up to 10 seconds, because MaxDelay caps every computed delay and the header is just one input to the backoff.
10 seconds, because the header value is clamped to MaxRetryAfter and replaces the backoff calculation.
